description: The bar chart illustrates five different parameter distribution patterns—labeled Increasing, Uniform, Decreasing, Spindle, and Bottleneck—each represented by a group of vertical bars that visually depict the relative magnitude of parameters across a sequence. The horizontal axis displays these five categories, each corresponding to a distinct distribution shape, while the vertical axis, though unlabeled, represents the magnitude of the parameters, with the scale increasing from bottom to top. In the "Increasing" pattern, the bars rise progressively from left to right, showing a clear upward trend in parameter values. The "Uniform" pattern displays bars of approximately equal height, indicating consistent parameter magnitudes across the sequence. In the "Decreasing" pattern, the bars decline from left to right, reflecting a downward trend. The "Spindle" pattern features shorter bars on the ends with taller bars in the middle, forming a bell-like shape. Finally, the "Bottleneck" pattern shows tall bars on the ends with shorter bars in the center, creating an inverted bell shape. All bars are rendered in a light green color and are positioned on a shared baseline, with the height of each bar corresponding to its respective parameter value within the distribution.
